Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

participant noun

also participants, partaker, those taking part, have a share in, be party to

classical

Cic. Att. 2.25.2: aut expediēs nōs omnī molestiā aut eris particeps
Ter. Heaut. 428: cujus maximē tē fierī participem cupis

particeps, participis

adjective and noun, third declension, one ending; + genitive · Wiktionary

sharing in, taking part in; as a noun, a sharer, a participant

The one who shares or takes part in something, with the genitive of what is shared: particeps cōnsiliōrum, sollicitūdinis, nūntiī. Near it stand socius, a partner or ally, and cōnsors, one who shares a lot or an inheritance (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • is quī interest — one who is present at or takes part in (+ dat.)

    phrase: intersum + dative (see be involved) · also used · classical

    For the people present at an event, a meeting or a game: quī convīviō, lūdīs, cōnsiliō intersunt, those taking part in the dinner, the games, the meeting.

Examples

  • quā rē advolā; aut expediēs nōs omnī molestiā aut eris particeps

    so fly here: either you will get me out of all this trouble or you will share itCic. Att. 2.25.2

  • Menedēme, salvē: nūntium apportō tibi cujus maximē tē fierī participem cupis.

    Good day, Menedemus: I bring you news you will be very glad to share in.Ter. Heaut. 427–428

  • cūr ego absum vel spectātor laudum tuārum vel particeps vel socius vel minister cōnsiliōrum?

    why am I away, unable to watch your successes, or to share in your plans, as partner or as helper?Cic. Fam. 2.7.2

See also be involved, member, associate, share.
